Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0188", "row_sha256": "503e74de58796fe09eb641f9c2e2e49db56d09e7ca50537a44e17e5eea969932", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you draft a short update for the Cedar Lane neighborhood weather station from these notes? yesterday was Tuesday, October 14, the gauge total was 8.6 mm, most rain came between 4 and 6 p.m., and a volunteer read the gauge at 7:10 this morning. the tipping-bucket gauge also had its morning calibration check; the log will say either passed or failed, so use that result to choose what to write. if the check passed, write a public update with yesterday's rainfall total and the timing of the rain. only give the total in that public update if the check passed. if it failed, don't publish or estimate any rainfall amount; instead write a brief internal maintenance note that identifies the failed calibration check and asks the next volunteer to recheck the gauge before any total is posted. don't make that note into a public announcement. use only the notes here, and output just one item, whichever applies: either the public update or the internal maintenance note. keep it concise, and don't include an explanation of which branch you chose.", "output": "Draft one concise item for the Cedar Lane neighborhood weather station, using only the information provided. The notes say that yesterday was Tuesday, October 14; most rain fell between 4 and 6 p.m.; a volunteer read the tipping-bucket gauge at 7:10 this morning; and the recorded total was 8.6 mm. Use the morning calibration-check result in the log to select the appropriate item:

- If the check passed, write a public update that includes yesterday’s rainfall total and when most of the rain fell. Include the total only in this case.
- If the check failed, do not publish or estimate a rainfall amount. Write a brief internal maintenance note identifying the failed calibration check and asking the next volunteer to recheck the gauge before any total is posted. Do not make this note a public announcement.

Output only the one applicable item. Do not explain which branch you chose."}]
